title: CREATE SCHEMA
description: Learn how to create a new schema in the current database using CREATE SCHEMA.

data.text: A schema is a collection of database objects including tables, views, triggers, stored procedures, and indexes. A schema is associated with a username known as the schema owner.

data.title: CREATE SCHEMA Syntax
data.content: Creates a new schema in the current database.

data.text: SQL Server provides built-in schemas such as dbo, guest, sys, and INFORMATION_SCHEMA. The sys and INFORMATION_SCHEMA schemas are reserved for system objects.
The following example creates a customer_services schema.

data.title: Create customer_services Schema
data.content: Creates the customer_services schema and a jobs table within it.

data.text: After creating the schema, you can find it under Security > Schemas in Object Explorer. You can also query sys.schemas to list all schemas.

data.title: List All Schemas
data.content: Queries all schemas and their owners.
data.code:
SELECT
    s.name AS schema_name,
    u.name AS schema_owner
FROM
    sys.schemas s
INNER JOIN sys.sysusers u ON u.uid = s.principal_id
ORDER BY
    s.name;

data.alt: SQL Server CREATE SCHEMA output showing the new schema

data.title: CREATE SCHEMA Key Points
points: Use CREATE SCHEMA to create a new schema in the current database.
Schemas organize database objects logically and provide security boundaries.
The dbo schema is the default schema for new users.
You can optionally specify an owner with the AUTHORIZATION keyword.
sys and INFORMATION_SCHEMA schemas are reserved for system objects.
